w10_T4_010276: An inventory started at 224 items. In the morning, 111 items were removed. The remaining multiplied by 5. By afternoon, 447 items were lost. By evening, the count tripled. When measured in triple-unit groupings (unit conversion), how many units total?

w10_T4_010283: A class had 118 students. In the morning, 8 more enrolled. By noon, 31 more joined. The enrollment multiplied by 5. By afternoon, it multiplied by 5 again. By evening, 12 more students arrived. When converted to five-student groups (unit change), how many groups were there?
w10_T4_010286: A budget started at 147 dollars. In the morning, 58 dollars were spent. By noon, 16 dollars were refunded. By afternoon, 10 more arrived. Then 114 dollars were withdrawn. By evening, the remaining tripled and was converted to fifty-cent units (unit change). How many fifty-cent units?
w10_T4_010289: A company had 114 employees initially. By morning, 58 more were hired. By midday, 24 were laid off. By afternoon, 38 left voluntarily. w10_T4_010296: A store had 219 items initially. In the morning, 46 items arrived. By noon, 14 more came in. By afternoon, the inventory multiplied by 7. By evening, it doubled. His associate store had 150 items. How many items was the final count (measured in double-batch units)?
w10_T4_010301: A project budget was 205 dollars. In the morning, 53 dollars were added. By midday, the total multiplied by 9 (for growth). By afternoon, 259 dollars were spent. w10_T4_010304: A small business started with 21 units. In the morning, 73 units were added. By noon, the inventory multiplied by 5. By afternoon, it multiplied by 9 (for bulk sales). w10_T4_010305: An inventory had 150 items initially. In the morning, 27 were removed. By noon, 20 more were taken out. By afternoon, the remaining multiplied by 8. Then 608 items were lost. w10_T4_010306: A storage started with 83 units. In the morning, 61 were added. By noon, 39 more arrived. By afternoon, 59 were added. The total multiplied by 4. By evening, 44 more units came in. When measured in 4-unit packages (unit conversion), how many packages were there?
w10_T4_010309: A team had 179 members in the morning. By mid-morning, 36 left. By noon, another 120 departed. By afternoon, 5 more left. By evening, 9 more were gone. The final count doubled. w10_T4_010312: A line had 90 items initially. By morning, 4 more arrived. It multiplied by 2 (doubling). Then by 7 (in groups of 7). At lunch, it was divided in half. w10_T4_010313: A quantity was 125 units initially. It was divided by 5 (into 5 parts, giving 25 each). Then 1 was subtracted. The result divided by 6. Finally, it doubled. How many half-units were in the final count?
w10_T4_010316: A warehouse had 56 items. In the morning, 10 were removed. By afternoon, the remaining multiplied by 9. Then 104 items were removed. By late afternoon, 57 arrived. w10_T4_010320: A company had 236 units initially. In the morning, 61 were lost. By midday, 90 more were lost. The remaining tripled. By afternoon, 57 units arrived. By evening, the count quadrupled. A distractor: a related branch had 110 units. What was the final total?
w10_T4_010322: A production run had 112 units. By morning, it multiplied by 7 (efficiency). By midday, 680 units were removed. By afternoon, it doubled. By late afternoon, it doubled again. w10_T4_010324: A workforce had 188 people initially. In the morning, 32 more joined. The group was divided into 4 equal teams. Each team had 3 new members added. By afternoon, the total multiplied by 9. By evening, 133 left. His sister's team had 75 people. How many final people were in the group?
w10_T4_010325: An investment started at 209 dollars. By morning, it multiplied by 5 (gains). By midday, it doubled. Then 26 dollars in interest were added. By afternoon, 209 dollars were withdrawn. w10_T4_010330: A budget had 130 dollars initially. By morning, 52 dollars were added. By noon, 27 more arrived. By afternoon, 179 dollars were spent. By evening, 4 dollars were deducted. When converted to 5-dollar bills (unit change), how many bills total?
w10_T4_010333: A task list had 97 items in the morning. It multiplied by 6 (priority escalation). By afternoon, it was divided by 3 (consolidation). Then 36 items were added. By evening, 39 more were added. When the total was measured in hours (unit conversion), what was the count?
w10_T4_010336: A project had 239 tasks in the morning. By mid-morning, 160 were completed. By noon, 21 more arrived. By afternoon, 51 more were assigned. By evening, 23 were removed. A distractor: another project had 115 tasks. How many final tasks were pending?
w10_T4_010346: A collection had 113 items. In the morning, 14 were sold. By afternoon, the remaining tripled. By late afternoon, 80 items were removed. By evening, 216 more were taken. The final amount multiplied by 5 (for storage calculation). How many (in five-item packs)?
w10_T4_010349: A stock had 181 units initially. In the morning, 88 were sold. By afternoon, the remaining quadrupled. Then 48 units arrived. By evening, the total multiplied by 7 and was measured in 7-unit bundles (unit conversion). How many final bundles?
